posts.title: Why Is My FPS So Low? 7 Fixes That Actually Work
posts.description: Low FPS on a good PC? 7 checks that fix bottlenecks, background apps and settings — plus how many FPS you should get.
posts.body:
Low FPS has a short list of usual suspects. Before spending money on new hardware, work through these seven checks — most frame-rate problems are solved by step three.

1. Find your bottleneck first

Every low-FPS story starts with one question: is your CPU or your GPU holding you back? Run your exact parts through our bottleneck calculator for your game. Upgrading the wrong component is the most expensive mistake in PC gaming.

2. Check what is running in the background

Browser tabs with video, Discord hardware acceleration, and Windows Game Bar recording silently eat CPU and GPU time. Close them, retest, and compare against your estimated FPS — if the numbers suddenly match, you found it.

3. Upscaling is free performance

If your game supports DLSS or FSR, quality upscaling mode typically buys 15-25% more frames for image quality most people cannot tell apart. Check Warzone or Cyberpunk 2077 on your hardware to see the exact gain before touching anything else.

4. Shadows and volumetrics first

Across hundreds of games in our database, shadows and volumetric lighting cost the most frames per unit of visual quality. Drop those two before anything else. Our settings optimizer walks through the exact order for your target FPS.

5. RAM running in single channel

One stick of RAM instead of two can cost 10-20% of your FPS in CPU-heavy games like Fortnite endgames. Check that your memory runs in dual channel — it is a free fix if you already own two sticks.

6. Thermal throttling

A dusty cooler or dried thermal paste makes your GPU quietly downclock. If FPS starts fine and decays over 20 minutes, watch temperatures, not settings.

7. Storage stutter in open worlds

Open-world streaming on a spinning hard drive causes hitching no setting can fix. An SSD is the cheapest meaningful upgrade for games like Cyberpunk 2077.

Still stuck? Plug your parts into the FPS calculator to see what your PC should be doing — then the gap tells you where to look.

posts.title: Cyberpunk 2077 FPS Guide: Best Settings for Any GPU
posts.description: The exact settings order to go from slideshow to smooth in Night City, plus what FPS to expect on five PC tiers.
posts.body:
Cyberpunk 2077 is the heaviest game in our database: 16GB of RAM and 8GB of VRAM, with ray tracing able to halve your frame rate. Here is how to tame it in order of impact.

What to expect on your hardware

Check the Cyberpunk 2077 estimates across five PC tiers first so you know whether your numbers are normal. A mid-range PC lands around 85 FPS at 1080p High — if you are far below that, something else is wrong (see our low-FPS checklist).

Step 1: Upscaling on, always

Cyberpunk supports both DLSS and FSR. Quality mode is worth 15-20% more frames and the game was practically designed around it. This single toggle outweighs every other setting combined.

Step 2: Ray tracing off (unless 40-series+)

Path tracing is a luxury for top-tier cards only. Turning ray tracing off is routinely worth 40% more frames — the difference between 35 and 60 FPS on mid-range hardware.

Step 3: Volumetrics and shadows down

Volumetric fog and cloud quality plus shadow resolution are the two raster settings that cost the most in Night City's neon streets. Drop volumetrics to medium and shadows to high before touching textures — texture quality barely affects FPS if your VRAM covers it.

Step 4: Match settings to your tier

Run your exact GPU and CPU through the FPS calculator with Cyberpunk preselected to see your numbers at every preset, or tell the optimizer your target FPS and it will walk the whole order for you.

Rule of thumb: upscaling quality plus no ray tracing plus medium volumetrics gets almost any 8GB card to a locked 60 at 1080p.

posts.title: Valorant Low FPS on a Good PC? It Is Probably Your CPU
posts.description: Valorant runs on almost anything, so low FPS on strong hardware almost always means one thing. Here is the fix.
posts.body:
Valorant needs just 8GB of RAM and 1GB of VRAM — so if your good PC stutters, your graphics card is innocent. Valorant is one of the most CPU-bound games we track, and the fix is different from most shooters.

Confirm it in 30 seconds

Put your parts into the bottleneck calculator for Valorant. Nine times out of ten it reports a CPU bottleneck above 30%. That is normal for this game — it means frames scale with single-core CPU speed, not GPU power.

What actually helps

First, check your numbers against the Valorant estimates for your tier. Then: run dual-channel RAM (single channel costs real frames here), cap background CPU usage, and keep Windows power mode on Best Performance. There is no DLSS or FSR in Valorant, so resolution is your only render lever — dropping to lower resolution helps weak integrated graphics a lot.

Settings barely matter — and that is the point

Unlike heavy single-player games, Valorant's settings change FPS by single-digit percentages. Competitive players run everything low for visibility and frame-time stability, not because their GPU needs it. If you came from Counter-Strike 2 with the same symptoms, the same CPU-first logic applies.

Bottom line: in Valorant, a mid-range GPU with a fast CPU beats an expensive GPU with a slow CPU every time. Verify with the calculator before spending anything.
